final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic core repack in the HA2 stalk; reduces packing strain minimally while staying far from the cleavage site and receptor-binding head, preserving cell entry.
Slightly larger hydrophobe in the stalk coiled-coil could improve core packing and thermal stability with low risk to fusion function.
Ala-to-Leu cavity filling in the HA2 core is a classic thermostabilization strategy; modest confidence due to unverified structural context.

stop_reason.detail: Self-iteration has converged on a stable Top-3 of conservative stalk-packing mutations; no further gains expected without structural evidence tools.

history.rationale: Conservative hydrophobic substitution in the HA2 stalk region that may modestly improve core packing without directly touching cleavage, fusion peptide, or receptor-binding residues. Expected low risk to cell entry because it is a similar branched hydrophobe.
Conservative hydrophobic core repack in HA2 stalk; I->V reduces cavity/packing strain minimally and is far from the cleavage site and receptor-binding head, so cell entry should be preserved.
Leucine substitution in the stem helical region could add hydrophobic bulk and stabilizing van der Waals contacts. Conservative chemistry makes viability disruption unlikely.
Larger hydrophobe in the stalk coiled-coil region could improve packing and thermal stability with low risk to fusion function.
Removing a polar side chain near the HA2 helix bundle may reduce local flexibility while retaining small size. This is distant from known entry-critical cleavage and receptor sites.
Removing an exposed polar Ser for Ala adds slight hydrophobic stability; risk of losing a key H-bond is modest.
Conservative beta-branched hydrophobe swap in the membrane-proximal ectodomain that may tune packing near the stem base. Likely tolerated, though benefits may be modest.
Conservative substitution in the membrane-proximal region; plausible but close to TM anchor where stability gains matter less.
Isoleucine for leucine preserves hydrophobicity while potentially improving side-chain packing in a helical/anchoring segment. Low expected effect on receptor engagement.
Nearly isosteric swap near the TM domain; marginal effect on soluble HA stability, demoted slightly.
Alanine-to-leucine adds hydrophobic volume in the long HA2 coiled-coil region, which can increase thermal stability if space permits. Some overpacking risk keeps confidence moderate.
Ala->Leu cavity fill in the HA2 core is a classic thermostabilizing strategy; promoted above L532I given better structural rationale.
Lysine-to-arginine is conservative and may strengthen electrostatics/H-bond networks in the stalk. Likely neutral for entry but uncertain for stability.
Surface charge swap offers negligible folding stability gain; dropped to focus pool on packing-improving candidates.

rejection.reason: Surface charge swap offers negligible folding stability gain; dropped to focus pool on packing-improving candidates.

history.rationale: Removing a solvent-exposed negative charge could reduce local repulsion or flexibility in the stem region. Risk includes loss of a favorable salt bridge, so confidence is limited.
Removing a surface Glu risks losing stabilizing salt bridges; uncertain net effect, reject.

rejection.reason: Removing a surface Glu risks losing stabilizing salt bridges; uncertain net effect, reject.

history.rationale: A conservative added methyl group in the membrane-proximal ectodomain may improve hydrophobic packing. Not expected to impair entry directly.
Mildly stabilizing but membrane-proximal; keep as backup.
Glycine-to-alanine can stiffen a flexible segment and raise thermostability, but backbone constraints near the stem base make this comparatively risky.
Glycine position may confer required flexibility near the TM anchor; backbone restriction risk outweighs stability gain.

rejection.reason: Glycine position may confer required flexibility near the TM anchor; backbone restriction risk outweighs stability gain.
